# zyxel_cloudflare_ipv4_ranges (Data Source)

Reads Cloudflare's official IPv4 range list over HTTP(S) during planning, so firewall rules can follow the published list instead of a hardcoded copy.

The data source performs one unauthenticated `GET` request with a 20-second timeout and a normal `User-Agent`. It does not use the router client or send cookies, so it works even when the provider is configured only for this lookup. A non-2xx response, an oversized body, or an unexpected entry fails the plan with a diagnostic instead of returning a partial list.

Every non-blank line must be a canonical IPv4 CIDR: `net/netip` parsing must yield an IPv4 address, the prefix must already be its masked network address, and at least two ranges are required. IPv6 entries, host bits, missing prefix lengths, duplicate entries, and HTML error pages are rejected. Ranges are returned in source order and are never sorted or rewritten.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "zyxel_cloudflare_ipv4_ranges" "cloudflare" {}

output "cloudflare_ipv4_ranges" {
  value = data.zyxel_cloudflare_ipv4_ranges.cloudflare.ranges
}
```

Terraform reads the data source during each plan, so plan output changes when Cloudflare updates the list. Reference it directly to build rule inputs. These accepts alone do not deny other sources; use `zyxel_acl_policy` for an ordered allow/drop policy. Choose unused ACL positions and replace the documentation address before applying:

```terraform
data "zyxel_cloudflare_ipv4_ranges" "cloudflare" {}

resource "zyxel_acl_rule" "cloudflare" {
  for_each = toset(data.zyxel_cloudflare_ipv4_ranges.cloudflare.ranges)

  name              = "Cloudflare-${replace(each.value, "/", "-")}"
  action            = "accept"
  protocol          = "tcp"
  source_cidr       = each.value
  destination_cidr  = "192.0.2.20/32"
  destination_ports = "443"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `url` (String) Absolute `http` or `https` URL of the IPv4 range list. Defaults to `https://www.cloudflare.com/ips-v4`. A change produces a new read during the next plan.

### Read-Only

- `ranges` (List of String) Canonical IPv4 CIDRs in the exact order the source returned them. Values are validated but never sorted, deduplicated, or rewritten.
- `source` (String) URL the ranges were actually read from, including any redirects.
